entries.test: Public pricing changes, financial disclosures and enterprise purchasing decisions would show whether cash burn forces increases that enterprise customers cannot justify.
entries.note: He quotes and reaffirms his own earlier prediction.

entries.test: Industry financial disclosures and customer-facing pricing information could be compared with documented costs and losses to assess whether they obscure weak economics.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion gives obfuscation a concrete financial meaning.

entries.test: Public loan exposures and financing agreements would show whether AI businesses depend substantially on financing from these banks.
entries.note: Points of failure refers to concentrated financing dependencies.

entries.test: Venture fundraising, investment exits and AI funding requirements would show whether liquidity constraints prevent continued support of AI losses.
entries.note: The claim asserts a present financing constraint and its consequence.

entries.test: Financial results across hardware sellers, compute providers, AI labs and application startups would establish which links are profitable.
Project financing terms, construction and operating costs, and contracted customer payments would establish profitability for occupied AI data centers.
entries.note: This is an economic calculation, not an inherently inaccessible counterfactual.

entries.test: Global project construction records and loan schedules as of publication would establish capacity under construction and interest-only payment arrangements.
entries.note: The normalization adds 'about' to an unqualified 5GW figure.

entries.test: GPU compute providers' reported revenues, expenses and margins would establish whether the business has low or negative margins.
entries.note: 'All evidence points to' presents an affirmative evidential conclusion.

entries.test: AI labs' compute contracts and financial disclosures would establish the frequency and scale of upfront payments alongside ongoing expenses.
Public financial results, unit economics and credible operating projections would show whether either company has an economically feasible route to profitability.
entries.note: A firm business viability claim is checkable despite uncertainty in projections.

entries.test: AI startups' financial results and model sourcing disclosures would establish whether any profitable or independently modeled startup contradicts the universal claim.
Subscription interfaces, usage records and applicable token prices for his identified examples would establish disclosure quality and token value relative to fees.
entries.note: The normalization drops 'for the most part' from the masking claim.

entries.test: Historical Anthropic subscription limits and documented usage costs would establish whether subscribers could consume upwards of $8 per subscription dollar.
entries.note: API retail value and actual compute expense must be distinguished.

entries.test: Public growth, financing and unit-economics data would show whether sustained external subsidies enabled growth of otherwise loss-making products.
entries.note: 'Infinite resources' has a plain contextual meaning of indefinite subsidy.

entries.test: Comparable coding workloads, token consumption, posted prices and serving-cost disclosures would show whether reasoning increases total costs despite lower token prices.
entries.note: The normalization broadens coding models to reasoning-heavy models and turns a lack of implication into a categorical denial of lower serving costs.

entries.test: Subscription unit economics and AI companies' revenue and loss statements would establish whether monthly pricing is viable and whether every company loses heavily.
Cursor's funding history and cumulative recognized revenue through publication would establish the stated totals.
entries.note: The normalization omits the explicit linear-growth assumption underlying the revenue estimate.

entries.test: Labs' financing and capacity constraints, pricing histories and documented reasons for changes would establish whether those pressures drive price increases.
Startup pricing, service changes and churn following supplier price increases would establish the asserted causal sequence.
Supplier revenue, startup model migrations and business failures following price hikes would test the claimed inevitable effects.
Historical product revenue and attributable delivery costs would establish whether AI labs consistently subsidized their products.
Cursor's enterprise segment margins and documented customer usage costs relative to subscription payments would establish enterprise profitability.
entries.note: The extracted proposition captures his rejection of Cursor's claim, not his endorsement of it.

entries.test: Historical and subsequent subscription allowances would show whether both companies substantially reduce available tokens.
Startup closures attributed to model costs and subsequent lab API revenue would establish the predicted collapse and revenue loss.
entries.note: The normalization narrows the claimed loss of model-access revenue to revenue from those startups.

entries.test: Subscription usage allowances, delivery costs and subscriber counts after cost-covering limits would establish the predicted reductions.
Compute commitments, utilization, financial capacity and published growth projections would show whether mistimed projections leave both labs with unaffordable surplus reservations.
entries.note: The normalization omits the asserted cause: mistimed growth projections.

entries.test: Industry financial results, unit economics and funding records would establish whether generative AI depends on speculative financing of persistent losses.
Historical technology business costs and current AI unit economics would test the claimed unprecedented costs and need for tenfold pricing or substantial usage cuts.
entries.note: The normalization adds approximation to '10x' and softens the specified severity of the rate-limit alternative.

entries.test: AI company acquisitions, public offerings, secondary transactions and documented exit prospects would establish whether most invested capital lacks a viable liquidity route.
AI startup valuations and financing conditions after a failed exit or firesale would test whether one such event breaks confidence in exit prospects.
entries.note: 'It only takes one' asserts sufficiency; the normalization weakens this to 'could'.

entries.test: AI companies' future inference expenses, profitability and intellectual-property holdings would test the predicted continuing losses and absence of IP.
entries.note: The normalization changes 'every AI company' to startups and weakens 'bereft' to 'little' IP.

entries.test: Company growth, venture funding, marketing expenditure and unit economics would establish whether subsidized spending was necessary for the observed growth.
entries.note: 'Unlimited' summarizes the asserted freedom to burn as much money as desired.

entries.test: Comparable subscription usage and cost data across providers would establish the $3–$13 ratio and whether these two labs offer the largest subsidies.
entries.note: Actual compute cost must be distinguished from the retail API value of tokens.

entries.test: Cursor's published plan prices and included token allowances would establish the claimed excess value per subscription dollar.
AI startups' pricing histories, usage limits and cost reductions during the months after June 2025 would establish how widespread austerity became.

entries.note: 'Likely' explicitly qualifies the prediction.

entries.test: Historical AWS buildout costs, Uber losses and AI companies' spending and growth would establish whether the specific economic analogy holds.
entries.note: The normalization broadens rejection of an economic analogy into general non-comparability and omits the historical scope.

entries.test: Uber and AI providers' financial statements would establish differences in capital requirements, marginal service costs and revenue models.
entries.note: The surrounding paragraphs specify the economic differences being asserted.

entries.test: Public inference revenue and attributable expense disclosures available at publication would establish inference profitability and whether supporting evidence existed.
entries.note: He endorses the denial, not the opening position he quotes.

entries.test: AI labs' subsequent operating records and accounting disclosures would establish whether training remains a recurring operating expense.
entries.note: The record combines a forward claim of persistence with a current accounting claim.

entries.test: Hyperscalers' debt issuance, cash-flow statements and AI revenue disclosures would establish both assertions as of publication.
Public AI investment commitments, operating costs and return calculations would establish whether $2 trillion of additional revenue by 2030 is required for financial viability.
entries.note: This asserts a financial requirement, not that the revenue will materialize.

entries.test: Posted token prices and independently reported serving costs would establish whether price reductions necessarily reflect lower production costs.
entries.note: The surrounding paragraph supplies the reference to falling prices.

entries.test: Reported advertising trial revenue and the cited 2026 revenue target would establish the monthly run rate and its gap from the target.
entries.note: The $8.3 million is a run-rate conversion, not necessarily revenue realized in every trial month.
The claim attributes a private purpose of deceiving subscribers; public limit changes alone cannot establish that intention.

entries.test: Funding announcements, campaign timing and public investor accounts would establish the round and whether the campaign contributed to securing it.
Published promotion terms, subsequent usage limits and access disclosures would show whether the sequence made actual subscriber allowances less clear.
entries.note: The extracted assertion concerns the effect on transparency, not the separately hedged 'swindle' judgment.
This introduces alternative scenarios without selecting an outcome.
The preceding introduction frames this as one possible scenario.
He presents this as an alternative possibility, not a firm prediction.

entries.test: Subsequent major price increases, usage cuts and other cost reductions at both labs during their IPO preparations would establish whether more belt-tightening occurs.
entries.note: 'I wager' expresses a committed prediction here; adding 'likely' weakens it.

entries.test: Both labs' financial results, viable operating projections and customer retention at cost-covering prices would establish the asserted losses and commercial unsustainability.
entries.note: 'Do not work' refers to commercial viability in context.

entries.test: Anthropic achieving sustained profitability or ceasing operations without doing so would settle the prediction.

entries.note: This is a broad moral characterization without specified acts or legal findings.
Whether the conduct deserves legal or regulatory action is a normative judgment.
The central commitment is what companies should have done.
The source makes a historical counterfactual about adoption under different prices; the normalization turns it into a general present claim.

entries.test: Public usage and serving-cost analyses by customer engagement level would establish whether the heaviest users cost the most to serve.

entries.note: Not seeing a solution reports his own assessment; it does not explicitly predict an unlikely outcome.

entries.test: Startup revenues, delivery costs and funding requirements would establish whether every AI startup has unsustainable unit economics.
entries.note: The surrounding explanation gives 'economically broken' a concrete cost-versus-revenue meaning.

entries.test: Subscription contracts, published usage guarantees and change policies would show whether subscribers have reliable assurance of unchanged workload support for three months.
entries.note: This concerns the predictability offered at publication, not a prediction that access must decline.
'One has to imagine' qualifies the projected future.

entries.test: 2025 AI revenue estimates and evidence of purchases at subsidized versus cost-covering prices would test the amount and exclusive subsidy dependence of demand.
entries.note: 'Only exists due to' is a causal assertion.

entries.test: Customer purchases and industry revenue after adoption of cost-covering prices would show whether AI demand disappears.
entries.note: This is a prospective condition that could occur, not an irretrievable historical counterfactual.

entries.test: Commercial adoption at profitable prices and the cost effects of forthcoming technical advances would test the asserted lack of an economic rescue.
entries.note: The normalization expands 'waiting in the wings' into an unrestricted denial of any future cost-cutting breakthrough.

entries.test: AI industry financial viability following Vera Rubin deployment or a systemic rescue would establish whether either averts the predicted economic collapse.
entries.note: 'Save' means rescue the industry's economics in context.

entries.test: Project announcements, construction records, financing documents and contracted demand would establish capacity totals and whether existing demand supports those projects.

entries.note: 'Mandate of Heaven' is a rhetorical characterization; the normalization removes 'I think' and substitutes a different belief.

entries.test: The labs' cash balances, burn rates and financing needs at subsequent price increases or service cuts would establish whether those changes signal cash shortages.
Big-tech capital spending, NVIDIA sales and AI investment contraction following any spending cut would test the proposed warning signal.
entries.note: The normalization weakens the exclusive claim 'only comes from' to general dependence.
A warning sign alone specifies neither a required subsequent outcome nor a time interval for assessing its reliability.

entries.test: Each named company's financial statements would establish spending or cash burn relative to revenue.

He lists an indicator without specifying what later outcome or interval would validate it.

No consequence or interval is specified for validating the warning sign.

'Shit is getting bad' does not specify a shared criterion for industry-wide trouble.

entries.test: NVIDIA's receivables, credit-loss provisions, cash collections and earnings reports following customer payment failures would establish the predicted deterioration.
Market price declines and volatility immediately following a NVIDIA earnings miss would establish whether markets react with substantial alarm.
